entities.summary:
Agustín Roberto Radrizzani (b. 1952) is an Argentine Salesian bishop who serves in Argentina, representing the Salesian congregation's extensive presence in Latin America's southern cone. Born in Buenos Aires, he was ordained a Salesian priest and eventually consecrated bishop within the Argentine Church's structures.

The Salesians of Don Bosco have been among the most important religious congregations in Argentina since the nineteenth century, establishing schools, technical institutes, and youth programmes that have served millions of Argentine Catholics. Radrizzani's episcopal ministry as a Salesian reflects this tradition of educational and youth-oriented pastoral work.

His ministry has been conducted in the context of Argentina's postconciliar Catholicism—navigating the complexities of Church-state relations under democratic governments following the dictatorship, engaging questions of poverty and social justice in one of Latin America's most economically volatile countries, and sustaining the Church's institutional presence in a society with both high nominal Catholicism and declining regular practice.
